SEARCH
Package Server

Class DBController

java.lang.Object
Server.DBController
public class DBController extends Object
singleton data-access layer for the GoNature server.

all SQL goes through this class. connection opened once by EchoServer.serverStarted(). URL and username come from /db.properties; password is supplied at runtime via setPassword(String).

method categories:

  • parks: getParks()
  • booking: getAvailableSpots(int, java.lang.String, java.lang.String), checkAndBook(logic.BookingRequest), addToWaitingList(logic.BookingRequest)
  • orders: getOrdersByVisitor(java.lang.String), cancelOrder(int), updateOrder(int, java.lang.String, int, java.lang.String)
  • auth: loginVisitor(java.lang.String), loginUser(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)
  • entry control: checkInVisitor(logic.EntryCheckRequest), registerExit(java.lang.String, int)
  • reports: getVisitorReport(java.lang.Integer, int, int), getCancelReport(java.lang.Integer, int, int), getUsageReport(int, int)
  • reminders: getTomorrowOrdersForReminder()

    • ORDER_EMAIL_SUBQUERY

      private static final String ORDER_EMAIL_SUBQUERY
      resolves a visitor's contact email at query time. orders.email was removed for BCNF normalization (email is functionally determined by visitor_id and lives authoritatively in the visitors / subscribers / guides tables), so order SELECTs derive it instead of storing it. drop this expression into any order query that aliases the orders table as o; it yields the same email column the result-mapping code already reads. lookup priority matches getVisitorEmail(java.lang.String): visitor → subscriber → guide, falling back to an empty string.

    • getWalkInAvailableSpots

      public int getWalkInAvailableSpots(int parkId, String visitDate, String visitTime)
      returns how many spots a walk-in may use at the gate right now.

      walk-ins are measured against the park's physical capacity (e.g. 100), not the lower pre-booking max_orders cap (e.g. 90). this is the gap that gives walk-ins the buffer: reservations can only ever fill up to max_orders, leaving capacity − max_orders physical spots that walk-ins can still claim — on top of any unused booking spots. so with 86 of 90 reserved, a walk-in sees 100 − 86 = 14 free.

      occupancy counts two disjoint groups so the physical limit is genuinely enforced (and back-to-back walk-ins can't blow past capacity):

      • pending/confirmed reservations whose visit-duration window overlaps visitTime, and
      • visitors physically inside right now (status completed, checked in, not yet exited).
      an order is in exactly one status, so the two branches never double-count the same row.
      Parameters:
      parkId - the park's primary-key ID
      visitDate - the date (today, yyyy-MM-dd)
      visitTime - the walk-in arrival time in HH:mm format
      Returns:
      free physical spots for a walk-in, or -1 on DB error or unknown park

    • checkAndBook

      public int checkAndBook(logic.BookingRequest req) throws SQLException
      Atomically checks slot availability and inserts a confirmed order in one transaction.

      Uses SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the parks row so that any concurrent call for the same park blocks at the DB level until this transaction commits or rolls back. Together with the per-park JVM lock in EchoServer, this eliminates the check-then-act race that could otherwise allow two visitors to both see one free spot and both succeed in booking it.

      Return value semantics:

      • >= 1: booking confirmed; value is the new order ID
      • 0: slot is full (capacity or max-orders cap reached)
      • -1: DB error or park not found
      Parameters:
      req - the validated booking request
      Returns:
      orderId on success, 0 if full, -1 on error
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a non-recoverable SQL error occurs (caller should surface it)

    • findAlternativeSlots

      public List<String> findAlternativeSlots(int parkId, String visitDate, String visitTime, int numVisitors, String visitorId)
      finds the 3 nearest slots to the requested date/time that this visitor can actually book for the same park.

      candidate slots are every standard hourly slot (08:00–16:00) over the next 7 days, ordered by absolute distance from the requested date/time so the closest openings are offered first. each candidate must pass both of these checks, which together guarantee that selecting it results in a confirmed booking:

      • park capacity — overlapping confirmed/pending visitors plus numVisitors must not exceed max_orders;
      • no self-overlap — the visitor must not already hold a confirmed or pending booking whose time window overlaps the candidate slot (mirrors the duplicate-booking guard in checkAndBook(logic.BookingRequest), which would otherwise reject the booking).
      Parameters:
      parkId - the park to check
      visitDate - the originally requested date in yyyy-MM-dd format
      visitTime - the originally requested time in HH:mm format (excluded)
      numVisitors - the party size that must fit in the alternative slot
      visitorId - the requesting visitor's ID, used for the self-overlap check
      Returns:
      up to 3 bookable alternative slots as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm" strings, nearest first; empty if none are available within the 7-day window

    • cancelOrder

      public logic.CancelResult cancelOrder(int orderId)
      cancels an order and notifies the first waiting-list entry for the freed slot. only pending/confirmed orders may be cancelled; completed/already-cancelled rows are rejected.

      cancellation frees up capacity: the slot is excluded from getAvailableSpots(int, java.lang.String, java.lang.String) so a new booking can take the vacated position. the freed slot is then offered to the earliest waiting-list entry for the same park/date/time via promoteFromWaitingList(int, java.sql.Date, java.sql.Time); if someone is promoted, their email is returned in the CancelResult.

      Parameters:
      orderId - the primary-key ID of the order to cancel
      Returns:
      a CancelResult indicating success or failure; on success, CancelResult.getNotifiedEmail() holds the promoted visitor's email or null

    • promoteFromWaitingList

      private String promoteFromWaitingList(int parkId, Date visitDate, Time visitTime)
      offers a freed slot to the earliest waiting-list entry for the same park, date, and time. on a match it creates a confirmed order for that visitor, removes them from the waiting list, emails them a real notification, and writes a server simulation log line.
      Parameters:
      parkId - the park whose slot opened up
      visitDate - the freed slot's date
      visitTime - the freed slot's time
      Returns:
      the promoted visitor's email address, or null if nobody was waiting

    • markNoShowsAndPromote

      public List<DBController.NoShowInfo> markNoShowsAndPromote(int graceMinutes)
      finds every CONFIRMED order for today whose grace period has elapsed without a check-in, atomically marks each as no_show, and offers the freed slot to the waiting list via promoteFromWaitingList(int, java.sql.Date, java.sql.Time).

      the UPDATE uses a conditional guard (status='confirmed' AND entry_time IS NULL) so a visitor who checks in between the SELECT and the UPDATE is never wrongly marked.

      Parameters:
      graceMinutes - minutes after the scheduled visit_time before an absent visitor is considered a no-show (typically 15)
      Returns:
      the list of orders that were just marked; empty if none detected or on DB error

      public boolean expireWaitlistEntry(DBController.PromotedEntry e)
      releases an expired promotion: cancels the held PENDING order, removes the waiting-list row, then offers the freed slot to the next visitor in line (which starts their own 1-hour window). idempotent; if the visitor confirmed first (order no longer pending), nothing is cancelled and false is returned.

      confirms a promoted visitor's held order, if still inside the 1-hour window. on success the held PENDING order becomes CONFIRMED and the waiting-list row is removed.

    • declineWaitlistPromotion

      public boolean declineWaitlistPromotion(int orderId)
      declines a promoted waitlist offer at the visitor's own request, before the 1-hour window expires. reuses the exact release path the timeout uses (expireWaitlistEntry(Server.DBController.PromotedEntry)): the held PENDING order is cancelled, the visitor's waiting-list row is removed, and the freed slot is offered to the next eligible visitor in line (starting their own 1-hour window). idempotent — if the offer is no longer live (already confirmed, expired, or handled), nothing changes.
      Parameters:
      orderId - the held promotion order the visitor is declining
      Returns:
      true if the spot was released and re-offered to the next visitor; false if it was no longer a live NOTIFIED promotion

    • confirmOrder

      public boolean confirmOrder(int orderId)
      marks a PENDING order as CONFIRMED; used when a visitor confirms an upcoming visit through the day-before reminder path.

      also deletes any orphaned waiting_list row linked to this order. this can happen when a visitor confirms a waitlist-sourced booking via the ordinary reminder flow rather than the dedicated waitlist-promotion dialog: confirmPromotedVisit is never called, so the WAITING row would otherwise remain indefinitely, leaving the two tables inconsistent.

      only rows currently 'pending' are changed; already-confirmed, cancelled, or completed orders are left untouched.

      Parameters:
      orderId - the primary-key ID of the order to confirm
      Returns:
      true if a pending row was updated to confirmed; false otherwise

    • calculateEntryPrice

      private double calculateEntryPrice(int parkId, String date, boolean prebooked, String orderType, int numVisitors, double fullPrice, boolean isGuide, boolean isSubscriber)
      computes the total entry price.

      Pricing rules (applied in order):

      1. GROUP by guide, pre-booked: guide enters free; the (numVisitors − 1) paying guests receive a 25% group discount stacked with a 12% advance-payment discount (0.75 × 0.88 = 0.66, i.e. 34% off).
      2. GROUP by guide, walk-in: the guide DOES pay (included in the headcount); all numVisitors pay full price less a 10% walk-in discount. Guide pricing is not affected by subscriber status; the guide path returns immediately.
      3. Base discount: pre-booked visitors receive 15%; walk-in visitors pay full price (multiplier = 1.0).
      4. Subscriber stacking: if the visitor is a Family Member Club subscriber, an additional 10% discount is applied on top of whatever base rate was calculated in step 2 (i.e. multiplied by 0.90). Examples:
        • Pre-booked subscriber: 0.85 × 0.90 = 0.765 (23.5% total discount)
        • Walk-in subscriber: 1.00 × 0.90 = 0.90 (10% total discount)
      Parameters:
      prebooked - true for a confirmed pre-booking; false for walk-in
      orderType - the visit type in uppercase ("SOLO", "FAMILY", or "GROUP")
      numVisitors - total visitors including any guide
      fullPrice - the park's per-person full price
      isGuide - true if led by a registered guide
      isSubscriber - true if the visitor holds a Family Member Club subscription
      Returns:
      the total price to charge

    • getCancellationDistribution

      public logic.ReportCancelDistribution getCancellationDistribution(Integer parkId, int year, int month)
      cancellation distribution: how cancelled + no-show orders spread across the seven days of the week for the given calendar month, optionally filtered to one park (otherwise the whole region). backs the day-of-week bar chart in the cancellation report and supplies the per-weekday and per-active-day averages.

      uses MySQL DAYOFWEEK() (1 = Sunday … 7 = Saturday) so buckets are emitted Sunday-first; weekdays with no cancellations are returned as explicit zero buckets so the chart always shows all seven bars. distinctWorkdays is the number of distinct calendar dates that carried at least one cancellation — the denominator for the per-active-day average, mirroring the operating-day denominator of getUsageReport(int, int).

      Parameters:
      parkId - the park to filter by, or null for all parks (whole region)
      year - the four-digit calendar year
      month - the month number 1-12
      Returns:
      a ReportCancelDistribution with all seven weekday buckets; an all-zero distribution on error or when the period has no cancellations

    • getUsageReport

      public List<logic.ReportUsageRow> getUsageReport(int year, int month)
      usage report: average concurrent occupancy per hour slot (08:00–18:00) for the given calendar month, per park. the client divides by capacity × 100 to get percentage-of-capacity for the line chart — i.e. how close the park came to its limit, so an operator can see WHEN it was under capacity (per the spec's דו"ח שימוש requirement).

      Interval-overlap occupancy: a visitor is counted in every hour H that their stay spans, not just their arrival hour — a visit with HOUR(entry_time) <= H < HOUR(exit_time) is "inside" during H. This is computed by cross-joining each order against an hours list (8–18) on that overlap condition, so a 4-hour visit contributes to four hour buckets and midday occupancy correctly accumulates across staggered arrivals.

      Denominator: each hour's monthly visitor total is divided by the number of distinct dates that hour actually had someone present (COUNT(DISTINCT visit_date) after the overlap join), giving the average concurrent occupancy on a day that hour was in use.

      only completed orders with both entry_time and exit_time recorded are counted, so future (confirmed) bookings never appear here.

      Parameters:
      year - the four-digit calendar year
      month - the month number 1-12
      Returns:
      a list of ReportUsageRow objects ordered by park name then hour slot; empty on error or no data

    • getVisitDurationByType

      public List<logic.ReportDurationRow> getVisitDurationByType(int year, int month)
      average-visit-duration report: the mean length of stay (in hours) for each visitor type during the given calendar month, across all parks.

      only orders that recorded both an entry_time and an exit_time contribute, so in-progress and future visits never skew the average. each visit's duration is TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, entry_time, exit_time) / 60.0 hours, and the order_type column is folded into two buckets — 'group' becomes "Group", everything else ('individual', 'family') becomes "Individual" — to match the "individual vs organized group" split the department-manager report calls for.

      Parameters:
      year - the four-digit calendar year
      month - the month number 1-12
      Returns:
      a list of ReportDurationRow ordered by visitor type; empty on error or when the period has no completed visits

      public boolean leaveWaitingList(int wlId, String visitorId)
      removes a visitor's own still-waiting entry from the waiting list ("leave the queue").

      guarded two ways so it can never delete the wrong row: the visitor_id must match the requester (you can only leave your own entry), and the status must still be WAITING — a row that has already been promoted to NOTIFIED (a held slot awaiting confirmation) is left untouched, since that must be released through the confirm/decline path instead. leaving a plain WAITING entry frees nothing, so no promotion cascade is triggered.

    • ensureVisitorRow

      private void ensureVisitorRow(String idNumber, String firstName, String lastName, String email, String phone) throws SQLException
      ensures a row exists in visitors for the given ID, inserting a minimal placeholder row if one is absent. this keeps the fk_guides_visitor and fk_orders_visitor constraints satisfied for IDs that were never formally registered as visitors (newly registered guides, anonymous walk-ins).

      must be called while a transaction is open (autocommit off) so the placeholder insert commits or rolls back together with the caller's own insert. it does not touch autocommit or commit/rollback itself; that is the caller's responsibility.

      Parameters:
      idNumber - the government ID to guarantee a visitors row for
      firstName - first name for a newly created row (NOT NULL in the schema)
      lastName - last name for a newly created row (NOT NULL in the schema)
      email - contact email, or null/empty if unknown
      phone - contact phone, or null/empty if unknown
      Throws:
      SQLException - if the lookup or insert fails, so the caller can roll back
